title: PowerPoint to Video Converter: What to Look For Before You Choose (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: Choosing a PowerPoint to Video Converter
bullets: What to look for before you choose
slides.notes: Every PowerPoint to video converter makes different trade-offs. Before you pick one, here are the questions worth asking, so the tool fits your work.

slides.title: Start with what the video must do
slides.notes: Be clear about the job first. Your audience, platform, update schedule and how sensitive the content is will make most of the decisions for you.

slides.title: Narration: record it or write it
bullets: Narration read from your speaker notes
slides.notes: If your deck changes often, narration from your notes is easier to maintain. Fixing a sentence means editing text, not recording it all again.

slides.title: Check files, design and story
bullets: Check your organisation's policy before you upload
Preview a real deck, not a demo
Does it rework the story, scenes and motion?
slides.notes: For sensitive material, check your organisation's policy on online tools before uploading. Then preview a real deck, and ask whether the tool improves it or just plays it back.

slides.title: Timing, captions, format and price
bullets: MP4 is the most widely accepted
slides.notes: Look for timing that follows the speech, captions for viewers with the sound off, an MP4 your platform accepts, and clear limits on price and watermarks.

slides.title: Test drive with your own deck
bullets: Ordinary slides in, extraordinary video out
Basic: try it, no subscription needed
slides.notes: Turn a real deck into video. On Pro, a.i. directs it, tightening the story and timing animation to your narration. Try it first on Basic at powerpoint2vid.com.
